transcription.notes: The entire single source page was read, including the English masthead, all four English tasks, equipment and time instructions, and the closing sentence and dated footer. Russian and English columns are parallel versions of the same four tasks; the English column is transcribed once without translating or duplicating the Russian version. The surrounding grid separates translations and instructions; it is not a numerical data table. Decorative logos and bears are not task figures. The bold emphasis on light, watch, α and 20 minutes and the bold italic closing sentence are retained. The source wording “You are provided by” is preserved. The header gives the overall Olympiad dates 22 – 30. IX. 2011; the page footer dates this observational paper 25.IX.2011, used for held. Both printed group codes α and β are retained. No school-grade equivalence is inferred. No points, official solutions, charts or external data sheets are printed or referenced. Tasks refer to the actual sky and telescope, so historical measurements and apparatus specifications have not been invented. Difficulty for task 4 is unrated because its actual apparatus and measurement procedure are not supplied.

problems.statement: Bring Jupiter to the centre of field of view of the telescope. Demonstrate the result to the examiner. Draw a picture with the positions of the moons of Jupiter at the moment of observation.

difficulty.rationale: With prior familiarity with telescope pointing and orientation, the task requires centring a known planet and recording the observed relative positions of its moons. This is a short practical sequence; the estimate assumes normal observing conditions and functioning apparatus.

provenance.evidence: The complete English statement of task 1 and the common equipment and time instructions were read from page 1 of the source PDF. No official solution is present. Ratings are preliminary content assessments relative to the listed prerequisites, not human calibration.

problems.statement: Calculate and write down on the paper the hour angle and horizontal coordinates of **α** Peg.

difficulty.rationale: With prior knowledge of the celestial sphere, hour angle and horizontal coordinates, the student must connect a named star and the local observing situation to several coordinates. The estimate concerns this combination of ideas, not an assumed school grade.

problems.statement: Draw and enumerate in descending order by brightness (1, 2, …) the eight main stars of the “Cygnus” constellation.

difficulty.rationale: With prior familiarity with the main stars of Cygnus and apparent stellar brightness, the student must identify eight stars, represent their relative positions and rank them by direct observation. The estimate assumes a sky in which the required stars are observable.
